questions.stem: An 18-year-old man was reviewed with recurrent fevers. He was known to have relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia. He had been treated 6 months earlier for a Mediport infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus epidermidis with cefepime and vancomycin. On this admission he was treated with gentamicin and meropenem for an ESBL-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia. Five days after meropenem was started, he spiked a fever to 38.5°C, and another blood culture was drawn. The blood culture signaled positive after 8 hours, and the Gram stain showed gram-negative rods.
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely pathogen?
questions.explanation: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia S. maltophilia is one of the few bacteria intrinsically resistant to meropenem. It is also intrinsically resistant to gentamicin. Malignancy and exposure to broad-spectrum antimicrobials, especially carbapenems, are risk factors for S. maltophilia infection. Meropenem is effective against ESBLs and wild-type B. cepacia, M. morganii, and P. aeruginosa. Gentamicin is effective against wild-type B. cepacia, M. morganii, and P. aeruginosa and some ESBLs. While any of those organisms can develop resistance to meropenem, the exposure to meropenem was fairly limited, and acquired meropenem resistance is uncommon in pediatrics.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 1 Q1

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man was diagnosed with pneumonia caused by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. He was known to have advanced HIV infection and was receiving ganciclovir for cytomegalovirus colitis and viremia. He had no known drug allergies. Investigations: Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL Hematocrit 24.8 Total white cell count 2.3 ×109/L Absolute neutrophil count 1.3 ×109/L Platelet count 110 ×109/L G6PD deficiency ECG: QTc interval 580 ms
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: Minocycline Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is intrinsically resistant to carbapenems (meropenem). Chloramphenicol would be considered risky given the patient’s pancytopenia. The patient’s prolonged QTc interval makes levofloxacin a suboptimal choice. Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole poses a risk of hemolytic anemia given the underlying G6PD deficiency. Minocycline provides activity against many strains of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and has no apparent safety concerns precluding its use in this case.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 9 Q3

A patient with enterococcus infective endocarditis has high level aminoglycoside resistance. What is one issue with using streptomycin?

questions.model_answer: a) Pneumocystis jirovecii (no TMP-SMX): (1) clindamycin + primaquine; (2) IV pentamidine (severe) or atovaquone (mild-moderate). Toxoplasma (no sulfadiazine): (1) pyrimethamine + clindamycin (with leucovorin); (2) pyrimethamine + atovaquone (or atovaquone monotherapy). Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (no ticarcillin-clavulanate or TMP-SMX): (1) levofloxacin; (2) minocycline (alternatives: cefiderocol, ceftazidime). b) High-level resistance to gentamicin does not predict streptomycin susceptibility, so streptomycin must be tested separately; and if high-level streptomycin resistance is also present, no synergy with a cell-wall-active agent is achievable in vivo (added issues: streptomycin toxicity and limited availability/level monitoring).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the streptomycin/high-level-resistance point is from this chapter; the PJP, Toxoplasma, and Stenotrophomonas regimens rest on standard IDSA/guideline therapy.

cohort_answer.text: PJP (no Septra): Severe: Pentamidine 4mg/kg IV, or Clindamycin 450mg PO q6h + Primaquine 15-30mg PO q24h x21d; Mild-moderate: Atovaquone 750mg PO BID with food x21d. Toxoplasma (no Sulfadiazine): Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h + Pyrimethamine, or Atovaquone 750mg PO BID + pyrimethamine. Stenotrophomonas (no Ticarcillin/Clav or Septra): Minocycline 200mg IV x1 then 100mg IV BID, or Levofloxacin 750mg IV/PO q24h, ceftazidime, colistin, cefiderocol. Streptomycin issue: high level resistance = growth in presence of high concentration of streptomycin or gentamicin, meaning no synergistic AG effect possible in vivo if resistant to both; cannot extrapolate resistance of one aminoglycoside based on the other

questions.model_answer: a) No. Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is intrinsically resistant to all carbapenems, including meropenem, because of its chromosomal L1 metallo-beta-lactamase (which hydrolyzes carbapenems). Meropenem should be stopped. b) Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) is first-line. c) Two non-beta-lactam alternatives with reasonable safety profiles: (1) Levofloxacin and (2) Minocycline.

questions.question: Regarding treatment of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.

parts.text: Which antibiotic should not be used for treatment regardless of susceptibility, despite breakpoints being available?
Explain why ceftazidime-avibactam and aztreonam are recommended together for treatment.

parts_raw.text: Which antibiotic should not be used for treatment regardless of susceptibility, despite breakpoints being available
Explain why Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Aztreonam are recommended together for treatment

questions.model_answer: a) Ceftazidime. It should not be relied on regardless of reported susceptibility because Stenotrophomonas commonly appears susceptible in vitro yet fails clinically; CLSI has withdrawn its breakpoints and it is no longer considered effective. b) Stenotrophomonas produces two chromosomal beta-lactamases: L1, a metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyzes ceftazidime (and carbapenems) but NOT aztreonam; and L2, a serine beta-lactamase that hydrolyzes both ceftazidime and aztreonam but is inhibited by avibactam. Aztreonam is stable to L1, and avibactam (supplied with ceftazidime) protects aztreonam from L2. The combination therefore allows aztreonam to evade both enzymes and reach the penicillin-binding proteins.
questions.beyond_mandell: IDSA 2023 guidance; L1/L2 beta-lactamase mechanism of the ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam combination.

questions.model_answer: a) Ceftazidime. Breakpoints are no longer supported and it is no longer considered effective, so it should not be used despite historical/available breakpoints. b) The combination overcomes the intrinsic L1 and L2 beta-lactamases of Stenotrophomonas. The L1 metallo-beta-lactamase hydrolyzes ceftazidime but not aztreonam. The L2 serine beta-lactamase hydrolyzes both ceftazidime and aztreonam but is inhibited by avibactam. Thus aztreonam, protected by avibactam from L2 and inherently stable to L1, bypasses both enzymes and binds the penicillin-binding proteins.
questions.beyond_mandell: IDSA 2023 guidance; L1/L2 beta-lactamase mechanism of the ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam combination.

cohort_answer.text:
Antibiotic you can't use: Ceftazidime - breakpoints are no longer available and it is no longer considered an effective treatment.
Ceftazidime-avibactam/aztreonam MOA: Used to overcome the L1 and L2 beta-lactamases intrinsic to Steno. The L1 MBL hydrolyzes ceftazidime but not aztreonam. The L2 serine beta-lactamase hydrolyzes both ceftazidime and aztreonam but is inhibited by avibactam. Therefore, Aztreonam-Avibactam bypasses inactivation and reaches the PBPs of Steno.

parts.text: Rate of resistance to carbapenems.
Mechanism of resistance to carbapenems.
Recommended treatment of Stenotrophomonas.

parts_raw.text: a) Rate of resistance to carbapenems
b) Mechanism of resistance to carbapenems
c) Recommended tx of Steno

questions.model_answer: a) Essentially 100%; Stenotrophomonas is intrinsically (universally) resistant to all carbapenems. b) A chromosomally encoded L1 metallo-beta-lactamase (zinc-dependent) that hydrolyzes carbapenems; contributory factors include reduced outer-membrane permeability and the L2 serine beta-lactamase conferring broad beta-lactam resistance. c) TMP-SMX is the treatment of choice. Alternatives/combination agents: levofloxacin, minocycline (or tigecycline), cefiderocol, or ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam. IDSA 2023 favours combination therapy (e.g., two of TMP-SMX, minocycline/tigecycline, cefiderocol, levofloxacin) for moderate-to-severe disease, or ceftazidime-avibactam with aztreonam when other agents cannot be used.
questions.beyond_mandell: IDSA 2023 guidance; L1 metallo-beta-lactamase mechanism of intrinsic carbapenem resistance.

cohort_answer.text: a) Intrinsically resistant to all carbapenems (intrinsic L1 metallo-beta-lactamase). b) Decreased outer membrane permeability makes it intrinsically less susceptible to beta-lactams and possibly fluoroquinolones; exhibits high-level resistance to non-antipseudomonal penicillins, cephalosporins, all carbapenems; production of intrinsic metallo-beta-lactamases (e.g. MBL-L1). c) TMP/SMX - treatment of choice; Levofloxacin; Tigecycline; Colistin. IDSA guidelines 2023: use two of TMP-SMX, minocycline/tigecycline, cefiderocol, or levofloxacin OR combination of ceftazidime-avibactam and aztreonam if significant clinical instability or intolerance/inactivity of other agents.

If the childhood immunizations were up to date except for the pre-school boosters, what would you do with regard to tetanus?
If the child had only received vaccines up to and including 4 months of age, what do you do for tetanus in this situation?

parts_raw.text: If no drug allergies, what is the preferred prophylactic antibiotic? (0.5)
If the childhood immunizations were up to date except for pre-school boosters. What would you do with regards to tetanus (0.5)
If the child had only received vaccines up to and including 4 months old - what do you do for tetanus in this situation (1)
If the child was HIV+ and immunizations and was UTD except for pre-school boosters, what do you do for tetanus (1)

questions.model_answer:
a) Amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (first-choice agent; covers Pasteurella, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus and anaerobes).
b) A puncture bite is tetanus-prone. With 3 or more prior doses (primary series done, only pre-school booster missing), give the due tetanus toxoid-containing booster; no TIG.
c) Vaccines only to 4 months = fewer than 3 doses: give tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine AND TIG, and continue/complete the primary series (an accelerated schedule can be used).
d) HIV positive (impaired humoral immunity): for a wound that is not clean and minor, give both the tetanus toxoid-containing booster AND TIG regardless of time since the last dose.
questions.beyond_mandell: Tetanus toxoid/TIG dose thresholds and the TIG rule for humoral immunodeficiency are from the Canadian Immunization Guide, not the Mandell text.

cohort_answer.text: Antibiotic: Amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (second line TMP/SMX or ceftriaxone + clindamycin, Redbook). Indications for prophylaxis: Immunocompromised; Cat bites; Puncture wounds; Hand, foot or genital involvement; Moderate or severe wounds especially with baseline edema/crush injury; Deep or surgically closed facial wounds. TIG only given if not received 3 dose series previously, or has humoral immune deficiency regardless of immunization status (including heme malignancies and HIV) if wound not minor/clean. Pre-school boosters missing: Give booster as due, no TIG. Only vaccinated to 4 months (2 doses): Need to vaccinate (restart series) and give TIG; can do accelerated course (4 weeks between doses 1,2,3 and 6-12 months between dose 3-4 and 4-5; dose 5 not needed if child over 4 years, so 3 doses 4 weeks apart then 4th booster 6 months later). HIV+ with pre-school boosters missing: Give booster dose and TIG. 'Individuals with humoral immune deficiency who have wounds that are not minor and clean should receive both TIG and tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine, regardless of the time elapsed since the last booster'

questions.question: An intubated patient develops ventilator-associated pneumonia due to Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and is currently on meropenem.
questions.question_raw: There is a patient who is intubated and develops VAP due to Stenotrophomonas (severity not specified). He is on Meropenem.

parts.text: Why is meropenem inappropriate?
What is the best empiric therapy for this infection?
He is unable to tolerate that drug. Name two non-beta-lactam antibiotic alternatives you can use that have relatively little toxicity.

parts_raw.text: Why is meropenem inappropriate?
What is the best empiric therapy for this infection?
He is unable to tolerate that drug. Name two non-beta lactam antibiotic alternatives you can use that have relatively little toxicity

questions.model_answer:
a) Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is intrinsically resistant to carbapenems. It carries two chromosomally encoded beta-lactamases: the L1 metallo-beta-lactamase (zinc-dependent) hydrolyzes penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems, and the L2 serine beta-lactamase hydrolyzes aztreonam and extended-spectrum cephalosporins. Meropenem is therefore predictably inactive.
b) High-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is the drug of choice and best empiric agent; for critically ill/severe infection IDSA 2023 favors combination therapy using two active agents (e.g., TMP-SMX plus minocycline or levofloxacin).
c) (1) Levofloxacin (fluoroquinolone). (2) Minocycline (tetracycline). Both are well tolerated relative to alternatives such as tigecycline.
questions.beyond_mandell: Provided context text is Mandell Ch. 221 (Burkholderia pseudomallei/mallei) and does not cover Stenotrophomonas; answer rests on IDSA 2023 Guidance on AMR Gram-negative infections.

cohort_answer.text: Meropenem inappropriate: Intrinsic resistance (L1 metallo beta-lactamase); S. maltophilia carries numerous resistance genes/mutations - L1 hydrolyzes penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems (not aztreonam), L2 has extended cephalosporin activity and hydrolyzes aztreonam; intrinsic aminoglycoside resistance via chromosomal acetyl transferase enzymes; multidrug efflux pumps reduce TMP-SMX, tetracycline, fluoroquinolone activity, chromosomal Smqnr genes further reduce fluoroquinolone effectiveness. Best empiric therapy (IDSA 2023 Guidance): 1) Use of 2 agents: TMP-SMX, minocycline/tigecycline, cefiderocol or levofloxacin; 2) Combination of ceftazidime-avibactam and aztreonam when significant instability or intolerance/inactivity of other agents identified. Alternatives if intolerant: Levofloxacin; Minocycline > Tigecycline

questions.question: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Septra). List four alternative drugs from different classes that can be considered.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Levofloxacin (fluoroquinolone). (2) Minocycline or tigecycline (tetracycline/glycylcycline). (3) Cefiderocol (siderophore cephalosporin). (4) Ceftazidime-avibactam combined with aztreonam (the aztreonam evades L1 while avibactam inhibits L2).

questions.question: A drug shortage occurs in your hospital.

parts.text: How would you treat PJP (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia), Toxoplasma, and Stenotrophomonas if TMP-SMX (Septra), sulfadiazine, and ticarcillin-clavulanic acid/TMP-SMX respectively were not available? Give two options for each.

parts_raw.text: How would you treat PJP, Toxoplasma, and Stenotrophomonas if Septra, Sulfadiazine, and Ticarcillin-clavulanic acid/Septra respectively were not available (2 options each)?

questions.model_answer: a) PJP without TMP-SMX (TMP-SMX is normally first-line): (1) IV pentamidine; (2) clindamycin plus primaquine [atovaquone or trimethoprim-dapsone are further alternatives, typically for mild-to-moderate disease]. b) Toxoplasmosis without sulfadiazine (standard induction is pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin): (1) pyrimethamine + clindamycin + leucovorin (preferred sulfa-sparing regimen); (2) high-dose TMP-SMX (an effective alternative for AIDS-related cerebral toxoplasmosis). c) Stenotrophomonas maltophilia without TMP-SMX or ticarcillin-clavulanate (TMP-SMX is the recommended agent, and TMP-SMX + ticarcillin-clavulanate has been used in cancer patients): (1) levofloxacin (fluoroquinolone); (2) minocycline or tigecycline.
questions.beyond_mandell: The chapter names only TMP-SMX and ticarcillin-clavulanate for S. maltophilia; levofloxacin, minocycline/tigecycline (and cefideromycin) as alternatives rest on IDSA AMR guidance, not this chapter.

cohort_answer.text: PJP (cannot use Septra): Pentamidine; Atovaquone. Toxoplasma (cannot use Sulfadiazine): Pyrimethamine + clindamycin + leucovorin; Atovaquone + septra + leucovorin; Atovaquone +/- pyrimethamine + Septra + leucovorin. Stenotrophomonas (cannot use Ticarcillin-clavulanic acid or Septra): Tigecycline (black box for death); Levofloxacin; Minocycline
